IS : 5379 - 1969

Indian Standard SPECIFICATION FOR AMMONIUM THIOSULPHATE, PHOTOGRAPHIC GRADE
0. F O R E W O R D 0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 13 November 1969, after the draft finalized by the Photographic Chemicals and Related Materials Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council 0.2 Ammonium thiosulphate or ammonium hyposulphite (NH 4 ) 2 S 2 O 3 is closely analogous to sodium thiosulphate or photographer's 'hypo' Ammonium thiosulphate finds extensive use as photographic fixing agent 0.3 This edition 1 1 incorporates Amendment No 1 (August 1986) Side bar indicates modification of the text as the result of incorporation of the amendment 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS . 2 I960* The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for ammonium thiosulphate used for processing sensitized photographic materials 2. REQUIREMENTS 2.1 Description -- The material shall be in the form of white or colourless crystals, soluble in water. 2.2 The material shall also comply with the requirements prescribed in Table I when tested according to the methods given in Appendix A. 3. PACKING AND MARKING 3.1 Packing -- The material shall be packed in polyethylene bag and repacked in air-tight containers or in such other containers agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )

3.2 Marking 3.2.1 The containers shall be securely closed and marked with the name and weight of the material in the container; manufacturer's name and trade-mark, if any, batch number, and the year of manufacture. 3.2.2 The containers may also be marked with the ISI Certification Mark.
NOTE -- The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act, and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder Presence of this mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard, under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control during production This system, which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer, has the further safeguard that the products as actually marketed are continuously checked by ISI for conformity to the standard. Details of conditions, under which a licence for the use of the ISI Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution

IS : 5379 - 1969 4. SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 4.1 The scale of sampling and criteria for conformity of the material to this standard shall be as prescribed in Appendix B.

APPENDIX
( CIause 2.2 )

A

ANALYSIS OF AMMONIUM THIOSULPHATE A-1. QUALITY OF REAGENTS A-1 1 Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and distilled water ( see IS . 1070-1960* ) shall be used in tests
NOTE � 'Pure chemicals' shall mean chemicals that do not contain impurities which affect the results of analysis

A-2. DETERMINATION OF AMMONIUM THIOSULPHATE A-2.1 Reagents A-2.1.1 Standard Iodine Solution -- Transfer about 13 g of iodine into a solution of 36 g of potassium iodide in 100 ml of water After solution is complete, dilute with water to 1 litre in a volumetric flask Transfer to a clean and dry bottle and store in dark. Standardize as follows Place about 0.2 g of powdered arsenic trioxide (As2O3), which has been dried over sulphuric acid in a desiccator for one week, on a tared 25 mm diameter watch-glass and weigh accurately Transfer the contents of the watch-glass to 500 ml glass-stoppered conical flask and dissolve the arsenic trioxide in a mixture of 25 ml of water and 5 ml of 10 percent sodium hydroxide solution If necessary, warm on a steam-bath to complete solution. Cool, acidify slightly with 6 to 7 ml of 10 percent sulphuric acid and add 40 ml of saturated sodium bicarbonate solution Titrate with the standard iodine solution adding 5 ml of starch indicator just before the end point is reached A-2.1.2 Starch Indicator -- Stir 5 g of soluble starch with 100 ml of 1 percent salicylic acid solution Add 300 to 400 ml of boiling water and boil until the starch dissolves Dilute to 1 litre with water. A-2.1.3 Methyl Red Indicator -- Dissolve 0.15 g of methyl red in 100 ml of water.
*Specification for water, distilled quality ( revised ).

5

IS : 5379 - 1969 A-2.1.4 Standard Hydrochloric Acid � 0 1 N. A-2.1.5 Standard Sodium Hydroxide -- 0 1 N. A-2.2 Procedure -- Accurately weigh about 8 g of sample into a 250-ml beaker and add about 100 ml of water Add a few drops of methyl red indicator and titrate the solution immediately to the first colour change with standard hydrochloric acid Dilute to 500 ml with water in a graduated flask and mix well Take a 50-ml of aliquot, add 75 ml of water, and 2 ml of starch indicator. Titrate the mixture with the standard iodine solution. Add dropwise, sufficient quantity of the sample solution just to destroy the blue colour, followed by a few drops of methyl red indicator, and titrate the mixture with standard sodium hydroxide solution to the first colour change A-2.3 Calculations Ammonium thiosulphate, percent by weight = where V1 = volume in millilitres of standard iodine solution (0.1 N) used, V2 = volume in millilitres of standard sodium hydroxide solution (0 1 N) used, and W = weight in grams of the sample taken for the test A-3. DETERMINATION OF SULPHITE A-3.1 Calculate the sulphite from the volume of 0.1 N sodium hydroxide used up in the determination of ammonium thiosulphate, as follows: Sulphite [as (NH 4 ) 2 SO 3 ], portent by weight where V2 = volume in millilitres of standard sodium hydroxide solution (0 1 N) used in A-2.2, and W = weight in grams of the sample taken for the test. A-4. TEST FOR ACIDITY A-4.1 A yellow colour should be produced on the addition of methyl red indicator to the sample solution A 5. DETERMINATION OF ALKALINITY A-5.1 Calculate the total alkalinity from the volume of standard 6

IS : 5379 - 1969 hydrochloric acid (0 1 N) used up in A-2.2, as percent ammonium hydroxide Alkalinity (as NH 4 OH). = percent by weight where V = volume in millilitres of standard hydrochloric acid (0.1 N) used in A-2.2, and W = weight in grams of the sample taken for the test (see A-2.2 ) A 6. DETERMINATION OF MOISTURE A-6.1 Procedure -- Weigh 20.000 g of the sample and transfer it to a 250-ml flask. Add 75 ml of benzene and distil into a Dean and Stark type distilling tube and receiver. Continue distillation till no more water collects in the receiver and then allow the contents to cool to room temperature The volume of water under benzene in the receiver shall not be more than 0 1 ml A 7. TEST FOR SULPHIDE A-7.1 Apparatus A-7.1.1 Nessler Cylinders -- 50 ml capacity. A-7.2 Reagents A-7.2.1 Alkaline Lead Acetate Solution -- Dissolve 10 g of lead acetate [Pb (C 2 H 3 O 2 ) 2 3H2O] in water to produce 100 ml Add sufficient 10 percent ( w/v ) sodium hydroxide solution to dissolve the precipitate first formed, and then add 5 ml in excess. A-7.2.2 Standard Sulphide Solution -- Dissolve 1.50 g of sodium sulphide crystals (Na 2 S.9H 2 O) in distilled water and dilute to 200 ml This solution should be prepared daily. Dilute 1 ml of this solution to 100 ml with freshly boiled and cooled distilled water. One millilitre of the resulting solution corresponds to 0.021 mg of (NH 4 ) 2 S. A-7.3 Procedure -- Dissolve 20 � 0.5 g of the sample to 40 ml with distilled water in a 50 ml Nessler cylinder, add 2 ml of the alkaline lead solution, dilute to 50 ml, and mix well At the same time, treat 4.5 ml of the standard sulphide solution, contained in another Nessler cylinder in a like manner A-7.3.1 The colour produced in the sample solution shall not be deeper than that produced in the control. 7

IS : 5379 - 1969 A-8. DETERMINATION OF INSOLUBLE MATTER, CALCIUM, MAGNESIUM AND AMMONIUM HYDROXIDE PRECIPITATE A-8.1 Reagents A-8.1.1 Ammonium Oxalate Solution -- 4 percent. A-8.1.2 Ammonium Phosphate Solution -- 10 percent. A-8.1.3 Ammonium Hydroxide Solutions -- 10 percent and 3 percent A-8.2 Procedure -- Weigh accurately about 10 g of the sample and dissolve in 75 ml of water Add 10 ml of ammonium oxalate solution, 4 ml of ammonium phosphate solution and 20 ml of 10 percent ammonium hydroxide solution. Allow to stand overnight If any precipitate is formed, filter and wash with 3 percent ammonium hydroxide Dry and ignite at 600� � 25�C for 4 hours Cool in a desiccator and weigh. A-8.3 Calculation Insoluble matter, calcium, magnesium and ammonium = hydroxide precipitate, percent by weight where W1 = weight in grams of the residue obtained, and W2 = weight in grams of the material taken for the test. A-9. DETERMINATION OF RESIDUE AFTER IGNITION A-9.1 Procedure -- Ignite 5 0g of accurately weighed sample in a tared platinum or porcelain crucible at 600� � 25�C for 4 hours. Cool in a desiccator and weigh. A 9.2 Calculation Residue after ignition, . percent by weight = where W1 = weight in grams of the residue, and W2 = weight in grams of the material taken for the test. A-10. TEST FOR IRON A-10.1 Apparatus A-10.1.1 Nessler Cylinders -- 50 ml capacity. 8

IS : 5379 - 1969 A-10.2 Reagents A-10.2.1 Ammonium Hydroxide -- 10 percent. A-10.2.2 Citric Acid -- 20 percent A-10.2.3 Hydrogen Peroxide Solution -- 15 percent. A-10.2.4 Dilute Hydrochloric Acid -- approximately 2 N. A-10.2.5 Thioglycollic Acid -- containing not less than 89 percent of thioglycollic acid (SH CH 2 COOH) A-10.2.6 Standard Iron Solution -- Dissolve 7 020 g of crystalline ammomum ferrous sulphate [FeSO 4 (NH 4 ) 2 SO 4 6H2O] in about 300 ml of water containing 2 ml of sulphuric acid, sp gr 1 84, and dilute to 1 000 ml. Further diiute 25 ml to 1 000 ml with water freshly as required One millilitre of the resulting solution contains 25 g of Fe. A-10.3 Procedure -- Dissolve the residue obtained in A-9.1 in 10 ml of dilute hydrochloric acid and heat to boiling Cool and make up to 50 ml with water Dilute 4 ml of standard iron solution also to 50 ml. A-10.3.1 Transfer a 10 ml aliquot of the test solution and the iron standard solution to Nessler cylinders and dilute to about 30 ml with water To both cylinders, add 2 ml of citric acid solution and 2 drops of thioglycollic acid. Mix, make just alkaline with ammonium hydroxide and dilute to 50 ml with water. A-10.3.2 The limit prescribed in shall be taken as not having been exceeded if the intensity of the colour produced in the sample solution is not greater than that produced in the standard A-11. TEST FOR HEAVY METALS A-11.1 Apparatus A-11.1.1 Nessler Cylinders -- 50 ml capacity. A-11.2 Reagents A-11.2.1 Ammonium Hydroxide -- 10 percent. A-11.2.2 Dilute Hydrochloric Acid -- approximately 0 1 N. A-11.2.3 p-Nitrophenol Indicator -- 0.25 percent aqueous solution A-11.2.4 Hydrogen Sulphide Solution -- saturated, freshly prepared. 9

IS : 5379 - 1969 A-11.2.5 Standard Heavy Metal Solution -- Dissolve 0.64 g of lead nitrate [Pb (NO3)2], in water, add 10 ml of nitric acid, sp gr 1 42, and dilute to 1 000 ml. Further dilute 25 ml to 1 000 ml freshly as required One millilitre of the resulting solution contains 10 g of Pb. A-11.3 Procedure -- Transfer 10 ml of the test solution ( see A-10.3 ) to a Nessler cylinder In another Nessler cylinder, place 4 ml of the standard lead solution To both, add 2 drops of p-nitrophenol indicator and make slightly alkaline with ammonia Add dilute hydrochloric acid dropwise until the colour of the indicator is just discharged, and then add 1 ml in excess, followed by 5 ml of the hydrogen sulphide solution. Dilute to 50 ml and mix well. A-11.3.1 The colour produced in the sample solution shall not be more intense than that produced in the standard solution. A 12. TEST FOR APPEARANCE OF THE SOLUTION A-12.1 A solution containing 250 g of the sample per litre in freshly boiled and cooled water shall, on immediate examination, be colourless and free from sediment other than slight flocculence.

APPENDIX
( Clause 4 1 )

B

SAMPLING OF AMMONIUM THIOSULPHATE B-1. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS OF SAMPLING B-1.0 In drawing, preparing, storing and handling test samples, the following precautions and directions shall be observed. B-1.1 The sampling implement and the containers for samples shall be such that the material has no action on them They shall be clean and dry B-1.2 Samples shall be stored in such a manner that the temperature of the material does not unduly vary from the normal temperature. Samples shall be protected from heat, light and accidental contamination B-2. SCALE OF SAMPLING B-2.1 Lot -- In any consignment, all the containers of the same size and drawn from a single batch of manufacture shall constitute a lot 10

IS : 5379 - 1969 B-2.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the lot to the requirements of the specification, tests shall be carried out for each lot separately. The number of containers to be selected for this purpose n shall depend on the size of the lot N and shall be in accordance with Table 2
TABLE 2 SCALE OF SAMPLING
Lor SIZE NO OF CONTAINERS TO BE SELECTED

N (1) Up to 25 26 ,, 50 51 ,, 100 101 ,, 200 201 and above

n (2) 3 4 5 6

B-2.3 The containers shall be selected at random from the lot and in order to ensure randomness of selection, random number table ( see IS . 4905-1968* ) shall be used In its absence, the following procedure of sampling is recommended Arranging all the containers in the lot in one order, start counting from any container as 1, 2, 3, . ., up to r and so on, where r is defined as the resulting whole number after leaving out the remainder when N is divided by n. Every rth container thus counted shall be withdrawn to give the required sample size B-3. DETERMINATION OF TEST SAMPLES B-3.1 From each of the containers selected according to B-2.3, a small representative portion of ammonium thiosulphate of about 200 g shall be drawn with the help of suitable sampling instrument B-3.2 Out of these portions, equal quantities of material shall be taken and mixed thoroughly to form a composite sample of about 500 g The composite sample shall be divided into three equal parts, one for the purchaser, another for the supplier and the third to be used as a referee sample. B-3.3 The remaining portion of the material from each container shall be divided into three equal parts, each forming an individual sample One set of individual samples representing n containers selected shall be marked for the purchaser and the other two for the supplier and the referee, respectively
*Methods for random sampling 11

IS : 5379 - 1969 B-3.4 All the individual samples and the composite sample shall be transferred to separate sample containers The containers shall be labelled with full identification particulars. B 4. NUMBER OF TESTS B-4.1 Test for the determination of ammonium thiosulphate content shall be performed on the individual samples. B-4.2 Tests for the determination of all other characteristics shall be performed on the composite sample. B-5. CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY B-5.1 For Individual Samples -- From the test results for ammonium thiosulphate content the mean ( .. ) and the range ( R ) of test results shall be computed (range being defined as the difference between the maximum value of test results) The lot shall be declared as conforming to the requirements for ammonium thiosulphate content if the value of the expression ( - 0.6 R ) as calculated from the test results is equal to or greater than the minimum specified. B-5.2 For Composite Sampling -- For declaring the conformity of the lot to the requirements of all other characteristics tested on the composite sample, the test result for each characteristic shall satisfy the relevant requirements specified.
